task: Generate locally attributable prose from one or more sources
evidence_unit: Concise source spans, including nonconsecutive spans
intermediate_representation: Ordered clusters of source highlights per output sentence
added_mechanism: Original three-stage selection/planning/sequential fusion; ICL copy checks and fine-tuned constrained span copying
evaluation: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, AutoAIS, human AIS/fluency/helpfulness and verification time
boundary: Already has intermediate planning, source matching and multi-document input. Local spans can omit needed context; MDS AIS is lower than ALCE in Table 3.
title: Attribute First, then Generate: Locally-attributable Grounded Text Generation

task: Flag defects in debt-buyer default-judgment requests
evidence_unit: Requirement-relevant quotes and tables, located on original PDF pages
intermediate_representation: Seven legal requirements decomposed into dependency-linked subrequirements and verified evidence
added_mechanism: Domain requirement queries; OCR-preserved tables; fuzzy/regex relocation and original-source copying; Satisfied/Not Satisfied decisions and review UI
evaluation: 188 cases with three-annotator majority labels; 66 law students randomized to unaided or assisted review; +5.3 percentage points accuracy and -25.9% time
boundary: The human study compares the complete assistant with unaided review; it does not isolate the AfG stage or compare with CyberCase. Older Stanford manuscript differs.
title: AI Assistance for Human Review of Default Judgments

domain: Consumer medical QA; style simplification; multihop QA
task: Compare extraction, quotation, paraphrase, entailment and abstraction under common source evidence
evidence_unit: Shared short source quotes; gold WebMD snippets for MASH
intermediate_representation: Quoted generation revised into other operating points using the same quotes
added_mechanism: Control abstraction degree; common evidence for comparisons; measure user utility and verification effort across task distributions
evaluation: 480 queries; seven systems; 31 MTurk annotators; fluency, perceived utility, citation precision/coverage and time to verify
boundary: Perceived utility is not medical correctness. It shares a paradigm rather than reproducing every AfG component; more abstraction can reduce coverage.
title: The Extractive-Abstractive Spectrum: Uncovering Verifiability Trade-offs in LLM Generations

task: Answer medical questions using patient data, reference literature and definitions
evidence_unit: Entities with name, UMLS type and generated context, plus reference/definition links
intermediate_representation: Three graph layers and hierarchical medical-tag summaries
added_mechanism: Patient-entity/source/definition links; U-Retrieval with top-down selection and bottom-up response refinement
evaluation: Nine medical multiple-choice datasets, two fact-checking datasets, DiverseHealth; long-form ratings by seven clinicians and five laypersons
version: Published ACL 2025 PDF, 25 pages; differs from early arXiv record
boundary: Section 3.3.2 uses ATTR-FIRST as a baseline. Core method is graph construction/retrieval, so it is not a confirmed AfG implementation. Graph links do not by themselves prove semantic support.
title: Medical Graph RAG: Evidence-based Medical Large Language Model via Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

task: Retrieve document pages and answer financial questions with visual citations
evidence_unit: Page images and supporting block bounding boxes
intermediate_representation: Retrieved page set; jointly generated answer and page/block coordinates
added_mechanism: Visual citation for tables/charts; financial arithmetic/time/multipage categories; page/block support evaluation
evaluation: 1,394 inspected QA pairs; retrieval ranking/recall; answer accuracy; page/block citation precision/recall with bounding-box and crop evaluators
boundary: Section 5.2 explicitly generates answer and citations simultaneously and credits VISA for visual citation. AfG is background, not its adopted sequence. Visual support is evaluated with a model, not guaranteed.
title: FinRAGBench-V: A Benchmark for Multimodal RAG with Visual Citation in the Financial Domain

domain: Sustainability reports; climate QA; general scientific QA
task: Train faithful evidence-based QA specialists and test domain transfer
evidence_unit: Relevant/irrelevant source paragraphs with author/year/page identifiers
intermediate_representation: Quality-filtered synthetic training examples; no separate inference-time AfG evidence plan described
added_mechanism: Source/format/entailment filters; joint agreement of two AttrScore models; explicit unanswerability; tests on ChatReport and ClimateQA
evaluation: Synthetic/in-domain and real-source out-of-domain evaluations; source quality and attributability, with human audits of filtering
boundary: No AfG or Slobodkin match in extracted text; do not call this a domain adoption. Source-conditioned cited generation and training-data filtering differ from selecting evidence before every answer.
title: Towards Faithful and Robust LLM Specialists for Evidence-Based Question-Answering

task: Build investigative actor/role/timeline reports from a large cross-device chat corpus
intermediate_representation: Per-part record-oriented summaries, then ordered cross-part synthesis
added_mechanism: Trace-ID policy; local-model context splitting; actor/role/timeline schema; facts/hypotheses separation; trace equivalence and validation during evaluation
evaluation: One simulated Crystal Clear case, seven devices and five local models; entity, role, timeline, trace-ID, factual consistency and reasoning dimensions
version: Fresh 10-page author manuscript; publisher bibliographic record is 1-11 pages
boundary: No direct AfG lineage established. Sections 4.1/4.5 conflict on manual gold validation; 4.5 says it was not performed. A one-case model-report reference is weaker than independent multi-case gold annotations.
title: Structured Report Generation using Local LLMs for Chat-Based Digital Forensics

task: Apply instructor-specific pedagogy and rubric to submitted artifacts
evidence_unit: Text spans, code tokens/lines, notebook outputs or deterministic test results
intermediate_representation: Response-specific subrubric without marks, followed by per-subcriterion evidence trails
added_mechanism: Separate rubric construction from scoring; marks/maxima/source/rationale/flags; score-bound/source-presence/incomplete-response checks; lecturer calibration
evaluation: Only indexed primary excerpts were accessible; do not treat abstract agreement figures as fully audited experimental evidence
method_pages: Indexed PDF p. 3, Sections 3.1-3.4; Appendix pipeline excerpt
version: Anonymous ACL submission; acceptance and stable bibliographic metadata UNCONFIRMED
boundary: Public PDF download returned HTTP 403/browser challenge. Direct AfG lineage is UNCONFIRMED. Source-presence verification is explicitly distinguished from semantic entailment.
title: Auditable Evidence Trails for Pedagogy-Grounded LLM Judging

domain: Web content and generative engine optimization
task: Repair webpages to increase their probability of being cited by a generative engine
evidence_unit: HTML structural chunks and source sentence/chunk indices in the evaluation engine
intermediate_representation: AfG sentence selection/clustering/generation engine; separate diagnosis, tool repairs and aggregated edits
added_mechanism: Citation failure taxonomy; diagnose-repair-retest loop with memory; localized editing; document-centric train/test query benchmark
evaluation: MIMIQ has 204 pages and 12,240 queries; citation rate and content preservation; AfG engine Table 2 increases 60.20 to 70.00% versus vanilla
boundary: The added algorithm optimizes source pages, not case judgments. Its faithfulness metrics assess preservation of edited webpage content, not entailment of generated claims. Ten topics are not ten separately engineered domain systems.
title: Diagnosing and Repairing Citation Failures in Generative Engine Optimization

task: Generate attributed sentences through executable text-operation programs
evidence_unit: Source sentences and nested generated sentences
intermediate_representation: One executable operation tree per output sentence, parsed through Python AST
added_mechanism: Query-specific instructions on extract/paraphrase/compress/fuse operations; explicit execution traces; localized entailment checks and candidate reranking
evaluation: ASQA, LFQA and MultiNews; answer metrics and document/sentence attribution F1; module-level refinement versus whole-answer refinement
version: arXiv:2506.14580v1, 27 pages; bibliographic lock records this preprint
boundary: Builds on explicit planning and SummarizationPrograms and discusses AfG. Main comparison is ALCE, not AfG. Neural module outputs can still be unsupported; trace is not a proof of semantic faithfulness.
title: GenerationPrograms: Fine-grained Attribution with Executable Programs

task: Train models to produce fine-grained grounding quotes followed by cited answers
intermediate_representation: GROUNDING output followed by ANSWER output within a trained model sequence
added_mechanism: Synthetic high-quality attribution data; grounding-guided SFT; consistency-aware DPO under shared oracle grounding
evaluation: ALCE ASQA/ELI5/QAMPARI; NLI citation precision/recall/F1 and task correctness; human quote/verification evaluation
boundary: No AfG or Slobodkin match in this PDF. Closely related grounding-first paradigm, not confirmed derivation. Fine-tuning already exists in AfG; the differentiating training addition is the consistency-aware alignment recipe.
title: Learning Fine-Grained Grounded Citations for Attributed Large Language Models

task: Reproduce, diagnose and improve citation-generation workflows
evidence_unit: Document/span/token attribution views and workflow data streams
added_mechanism: Citeflow module composition; Citefix interface; post-hoc attribution diagnostics; human-LLM workflow editing
evaluation: Eleven baselines including AfG on ASQA with GPT-4o and Llama3-8B; multi-round improvement of a self-RAG workflow
version: Published ACL 2025 system demonstration PDF, 12 pages
boundary: AfG is a reproduced workflow. The newly improved workflow starts from self-RAG, so it does not establish a specialized AfG domain adaptation or causal benefit of its UI.
title: CiteLab: Developing and Diagnosing LLM Citation Generation Workflows via the Human-LLM Interaction

task: Localize unsupported predicate-argument relations in generated text
intermediate_representation: Generated text decomposed into supported/unsupported semantic QA relations
added_mechanism: Fine-grained annotation protocol and parser; separate entity coverage from relation entailment; automatic NLI/LLM detection
evaluation: 3,098 QA annotations with three workers per instance; news, biographies and generative-search responses; balanced accuracy/AUC and correlation with human judgments
boundary: An evaluator rather than an AfG generator. Mention overlap or copied quotes cannot establish agent/recipient/time/cause correctness; automatic entailment models remain imperfect.
title: Localizing Factual Inconsistencies in Attributable Text Generation
